summary: Join our GIS training course to master land use planning and water management. Gain practical skills to tackle environmental challenges with confidence.
lede: Land Use Planning and Water Management Using GIS connects parcel change, watershed behaviour, and water availability through structured spatial analysis in ArcGIS Pro and QGIS. The course covers geodatabase preparation, coordinate reference system checks, DEM conditioning, slope and drainage analysis, land-cover classification, SCS Curve Number runoff estimation, and land-use suitability modelling. You develop a suitability map, watershed risk scorecard, metadata record, action roadmap, and stakeholder-ready reporting workflow using MCDA and OGC data services. AI-assisted classification, Google Earth Engine workflows, and OGC service publishing are introduced to support planning reviews, water-risk prioritisation, and cross-functional decisions.
audienceIntro: This GIS land use planning course suits professionals who already work with maps, spatial datasets, planning evidence, or water-resource decisions and need a stronger end-to-end workflow.
prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to maps, spatial data, or planning and water-resource workflows. Basic experience with ArcGIS Pro or QGIS is helpful, but advanced scripting is not required. No coding or programming is required for completion. Advanced topics such as AI-assisted classification and Google Earth Engine are covered at operational application or conceptual awareness level, while core GIS analysis exercises use prepared datasets and guided workflows.
